sentences.text: Tugulusaurus was an early alvarezsaur, a group of theropod dinosaurs, likely measuring between 1.9 and 3 meters in length.
The holotype specimen, which is the single known fossil used to define the species, included a femur about 215 mm long and a very short left first metacarpal measuring 26 mm.
The holotype skeleton represents the only known remains of the species Tugulusaurus faciles.
Its specific name faciles means 'easily moving' and refers to the animal's agility indicated by its delicate bones.
Paleontologist Dong Zhiming described the small theropod Tugulusaurus faciles in 1973.
The generic name Tugulusaurus refers to the Tugulu Group where the fossils were found.
The holotype specimen IVPP V4025 was found in the Lianmuqin Formation dating from the Barremian to Albian stages.
Tugulusaurus was likely an agile animal with long legs that aided in reaching high speeds to chase prey or escape threats.
As an alvarezsauroid, Tugulusaurus likely used its long claws to dig into wood or dirt to find food.
Dong originally classified Tugulusaurus as a member of the Ornithomimidae within the Coelurosauria in 1973.
In 2005, Oliver Rauhut and Xu Xing concluded that Tugulusaurus is a valid genus of basal coelurosaurian with unknown affinities.
A 2018 cladistic analysis by Xu et al. recovered Tugulusaurus as a member of Alvarezsauria.
Tugulusaurus lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately between 122 and 100 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
The time range for Tugulusaurus is from the Valanginian to the Albian, between 137.05 and 100.5 million years ago.
